nodes.summary: Let a Sigma protocol have a perfect special honest-verifier zero-knowledge simulator and a finite challenge set $\mathrm{Ch}$, and let $x$ have a witness. For every verifier $V^*$ (its challenge any function of the commitment and of its coins), every test $T$ of its view and every $k$, the rewinding simulator with $k$ attempts, which never sees the witness, and the real interaction produce views passing $T$ with…
nodes.title: Zero knowledge against an arbitrary verifier, one round

nodes.summary: Let a Sigma protocol be specially sound, and let $x$ be a statement with no witness. Then for every $m$ and every adaptive prover, two challenge sequences of length $m$ that are both accepted in all rounds are equal. In the first round both challenges are answered for the same commitment, and two accepting transcripts with different challenges would give a witness; the remaining rounds follow by induction.
nodes.title: At most one accepted challenge sequence

nodes.summary: For a Sigma protocol, a statement $x$, a prover whose commitment in a round is $a(\ell)$ and whose answer to a challenge $e$ is $z(\ell, e)$, where $\ell$ is the list of the challenges of the earlier rounds in order, and a sequence $c_0, \dots, c_{m-1}$ of challenges, the verifier accepts all $m$ rounds: round $i$ checks the transcript $(a(c_0, \dots, c_{i-1}), c_i, z(c_0, \dots, c_{i-1}, c_i))$. For $m = 0$ the…
nodes.title: Acceptance of `m` sequential rounds

nodes.summary: For a per-challenge simulator, a statement $x$ and a verifier $V^*$: draw the verifier's coins $r$ and a guess $e'$ of its challenge, let the simulator produce a commitment and an answer $(a, z)$ for $e'$ from the statement alone, and output whether $V^*(a, r) = e'$, together with the simulated view $(r, a, z)$. Each attempt draws fresh verifier coins together with the fresh guess, whereas Goldwasser, Micali and…
nodes.title: One rewinding attempt

nodes.summary: For a statement $x$, a witness $w$ and a fixed challenge $e$, the distribution of the honest pair (commitment, answer) when the prover's coins are uniform.
nodes.title: The honest transcript for a fixed challenge

nodes.summary: For a statement $x$ and a cheating prover with coins in a finite set: from its coins $r$ the prover sends a commitment $a(r)$; on a uniform challenge $e$ it answers $z(r, e)$; the experiment outputs whether the verifier accepts.
nodes.title: The experiment of a cheating prover

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol is complete if for every statement–witness pair in the relation, all prover coins and all challenges, the honest transcript is accepted.
nodes.title: Completeness of a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: Under special soundness, a statement with two accepting transcripts that share a commitment and differ in the challenge has a witness.
nodes.title: A witness from two accepting transcripts

nodes.summary: For a statement $x$, a witness $w$, prover coins $k$ and a challenge $e$, the honest transcript of a Sigma protocol is $(\mathrm{commit}(x, w, k), e, \mathrm{respond}(x, w, k, e))$.
nodes.title: The honest transcript

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol is perfectly honest-verifier zero knowledge with a simulator, a function of the statement alone, if for every statement–witness pair in the relation the distribution of honest transcripts equals the simulator's output distribution. Only the honest verifier, which draws a uniform challenge, is simulated.
nodes.title: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge

nodes.summary: For a Sigma protocol, a statement $x$ with a witness $w$, and a verifier $V^*$ that chooses its challenge as an arbitrary function of the commitment and of its own coins $r$: with uniform coins $r$ and uniform prover coins $k$, the verifier's view is $(r, a, z)$, where $a$ is the honest commitment and $z$ the honest answer to the challenge $V^*(a, r)$.
nodes.title: The view of an arbitrary verifier in one round

nodes.summary: If $g^q = 1$, Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol is complete: this is the acceptance of honest transcripts of the Schnorr scheme.
nodes.title: Completeness of Schnorr as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: From answers $s$ to the challenge $r$ and $s'$ to the challenge $r'$, the extractor outputs $(s - s') / (r - r')$, the Schnorr extractor; it ignores the statement and the commitment.
nodes.title: The Schnorr extractor

nodes.summary: If $g^q = 1$, Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol is perfectly honest-verifier zero knowledge with the Schnorr simulator: this is the simulation identity of the Schnorr scheme.
nodes.title: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge of Schnorr as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: Schnorr's identification protocol as a Sigma protocol, for a group element $g$ and an exponent modulus $q$: statements are group elements $y$ with $y^q = 1$, witnesses are discrete logarithms $x$ with $g^x = y$, the prover's coins $k$ and the challenge $r$ are residues modulo $q$, the commitment is $g^k$, the answer is $r x + k$, and the verifier accepts an answer $s$ to the challenge $r$ for the commitment $I$…
nodes.title: The Schnorr identification protocol as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: For the statement $y$ and the challenge $r$: draw a uniform answer $s$ and output the commitment $g^s y^{-r}$ with the answer $s$, computed from $y$ alone. It is the Schnorr simulator with the challenge fixed to $r$.
nodes.title: The per-challenge Schnorr simulator

nodes.summary: If $g^q = 1$, Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol is perfectly special honest-verifier zero knowledge with the per-challenge Schnorr simulator: for every challenge $r$, the answer $r x + k$ is uniform when $k$ is, and the commitment $g^k$ is then $g^s y^{-r}$.
nodes.title: Perfect special honest-verifier zero knowledge of Schnorr as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: If $q$ is prime and $g^q = 1$, Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol is specially sound with the Schnorr extractor: this is the extraction property of the Schnorr scheme.
nodes.title: Special soundness of Schnorr as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: The distribution of honest transcripts of Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol is the distribution of honest Schnorr transcripts.
nodes.title: Honest Schnorr transcripts

nodes.summary: The verifier of Schnorr's protocol as a Sigma protocol accepts exactly the transcripts that the Schnorr verifier accepts.
nodes.title: The Schnorr Sigma-protocol verifier

nodes.summary: For a statement $x$, a finite type $R$ of prover coins, an adaptive prover (commitments $a(r, \ell)$ and answers $z(r, \ell, e)$ depending on the coins $r$ and the earlier challenges $\ell$) and a number $m$ of rounds, draw $r$ uniformly in $R$ and $m$ independent uniform challenges, and output whether the verifier accepts all rounds.
nodes.title: The experiment of an adaptive cheating prover over `m` sequential rounds

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol for a relation $R(x, w)$ between statements $x$ and witnesses $w$ is a three-move public-coin protocol. The prover, holding $(x, w)$ and random coins $k$, sends a commitment $a = \mathrm{commit}(x, w, k)$; the verifier sends a uniformly random challenge $e$ from a set $\mathrm{Ch}$; the prover answers $z = \mathrm{respond}(x, w, k, e)$; and the verifier accepts when $\mathrm{verify}(x, a, e, z)$…
nodes.title: A Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: Run up to $k$ independent rewinding attempts and output the simulated view of the first successful one, or a failure symbol if all $k$ attempts fail. Goldwasser, Micali and Rackoff's simulator repeats until success ("DO FOREVER") and runs in expected polynomial time; the truncation trades perfect simulation for a failure probability.
nodes.title: The rewinding simulator truncated after `k` attempts

nodes.summary: Let a Sigma protocol with a finite set $\mathrm{Ch}$ of challenges be specially sound, and let $x$ be a statement with no witness. Then every adaptive cheating prover with coins in a finite type is accepted in all $m$ rounds of the sequential experiment with probability at most $1 / \lvert \mathrm{Ch} \rvert^m$.
nodes.title: Soundness error of sequential repetition

nodes.summary: If a Sigma protocol is perfectly special honest-verifier zero knowledge with a per-challenge simulator, it is perfectly honest-verifier zero knowledge with the uniform-challenge simulator built from it: drawing the prover's coins and the challenge together is drawing the challenge first and then the coins.
nodes.title: Special HVZK implies HVZK

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol is perfectly special honest-verifier zero knowledge with a per-challenge simulator, which receives the statement and a challenge $e$, if for every statement–witness pair in the relation and every challenge $e$ the honest pair for the challenge $e$ has the simulator's distribution for $e$. This is stronger than perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge, which only constrains a uniform challenge.
nodes.title: Perfect special honest-verifier zero knowledge

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol is specially sound with an extractor if from any two accepting transcripts $(a, e, z)$ and $(a, e', z')$ for a statement $x$ with the same commitment and different challenges $e \ne e'$, the extractor computes a witness for $x$.
nodes.title: Special soundness of a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge implies statistical honest-verifier zero knowledge with error $0$, with the same simulator.
nodes.title: Perfect HVZK is statistical HVZK with error `0`

nodes.summary: A Sigma protocol is statistically honest-verifier zero knowledge with a simulator and an error $\varepsilon$ if for every statement–witness pair in the relation, no test of transcripts tells the honest transcripts from the simulated ones with advantage more than $\varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Statistical honest-verifier zero knowledge

nodes.summary: The distribution of honest transcripts when the prover's coins and the challenge are drawn uniformly and independently: the view of an honest verifier.
nodes.title: The distribution of honest transcripts

nodes.summary: From a per-challenge simulator: draw a uniform challenge $e$, run the simulator for $e$ to get $(a, z)$, and output the transcript $(a, e, z)$.
nodes.title: The uniform-challenge simulator

nodes.summary: For a complete Sigma protocol with a perfect honest-verifier zero-knowledge simulator, and a statement that has a witness, every transcript the simulator can output is accepted, although the simulator never sees the witness.
nodes.title: Simulated transcripts are accepted

nodes.summary: For a complete Sigma protocol and a statement–witness pair in the relation, every transcript in the support of the distribution of honest transcripts is accepted.
nodes.title: Honest transcripts are accepted

nodes.summary: Let a Sigma protocol have a perfect special honest-verifier zero-knowledge simulator and a finite challenge set $\mathrm{Ch}$, and let $x$ have a witness $w$. For every verifier $V^*$ and every test $T$ of its view, the left side for one rewinding attempt and the right side for the real view. Taking $T$ always true, an attempt succeeds with probability exactly $1/\lvert \mathrm{Ch} \rvert$ whatever $V^*$ does;…
nodes.title: One rewinding attempt simulates the real view

nodes.summary: For a specially sound Sigma protocol and a statement $x$ with no witness at all, every cheating prover is accepted in the cheating experiment with probability at most $1 / \lvert \mathrm{Ch} \rvert$: for each commitment it can answer at most one challenge.
nodes.title: Soundness error for false statements

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of one rewinding attempt, for every verifier $V^*$, every test $T$ of its view and every $k$, the simulator with $k$ attempts outputs a view passing $T$ with probability exactly $\bigl(1 - (1 - 1/\lvert \mathrm{Ch} \rvert)^k\bigr) \Pr[T \text{ holds of the real view}]$. By induction on $k$: the first attempt succeeds and passes $T$ with probability $\Pr[T]/\lvert \mathrm{Ch} \rvert$ and fails…
nodes.title: The truncated rewinding simulator reproduces the real view

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
